title_en: Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning Enforcement Work by People's Courts (Trial Implementation)

articles.content_en:
II. Execution Jurisdiction

9. In the course of domestic arbitration, where a party applies for property preservation and the arbitration institution submits the application to a People's Court, the Primary People's Court at the place of domicile of the respondent or at the place where the property subject to preservation is located shall make a ruling and execute it; where a party applies for evidence preservation, the Primary People's Court at the place where the evidence is located shall make a ruling and execute it.

10. In the course of foreign-related arbitration, where a party applies for property preservation and the arbitration institution submits the application to a People's Court, the Intermediate People's Court at the place of domicile of the respondent or at the place where the property subject to preservation is located shall make a ruling and execute it; where a party applies for evidence preservation, the Intermediate People's Court at the place where the evidence is located shall make a ruling and execute it.

11. Handling decisions and penalty decisions lawfully made by patent administration authorities shall be executed by the Intermediate People's Court in the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government where the person subject to execution has his or her domicile or where the property is located, that has jurisdiction to accept patent dispute cases.

12. Handling decisions and penalty decisions made by the various departments of the State Council, the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, and the customs in accordance with laws and regulations shall be executed by the Intermediate People's Court at the place of domicile of the person subject to execution or at the place where the property is located.

13. Where two or more People's Courts all have jurisdiction, the party may apply for execution to one of the People's Courts; where a party applies for execution to two or more People's Courts, the People's Court that first dockets the case shall have jurisdiction.

14. Where a dispute over execution jurisdiction arises between People's Courts, it shall be resolved by the two parties through consultation; if consultation fails, the dispute shall be submitted to the common superior People's Court of both parties for designation of jurisdiction.

15. Where an execution case under the jurisdiction of a Primary People's Court or an Intermediate People's Court needs, due to special circumstances, to be executed by a superior People's Court, the lower court may submit a report to the superior People's Court for execution.

III. Application for and Transfer of Execution

16. A People's Court shall accept an execution case only if the following conditions are met:
(1) the legal instrument applied for execution or transferred for execution has already taken effect;
(2) the applicant for execution is the right holder determined in the effective legal instrument, or his or her successor or assignee of rights;
(3) the legal instrument applied for execution contains a content of performance, and the subject matter of execution and the person subject to execution are clear;
(4) the obligor has failed to perform the obligation within the period specified in the effective legal instrument;
(5) the case falls under the jurisdiction of the People's Court to which the execution application is made.
Where an application meets the above conditions, the People's Court shall docket the case within seven days; where any of the above conditions is not met, it shall rule within seven days not to accept the application.

17. Execution of an effective legal instrument shall generally be applied for by the party according to law.
Legal instruments that have taken legal effect and contain content for payment of alimony, support, or maintenance, civil sanction decision letters, as well as criminal incidental civil judgments, rulings, and mediation agreements, shall be transferred by the trial division to the execution organ for execution.

18. To apply for execution, the following documents and certificates shall be submitted to the People's Court:
(1) A written application for execution. The application for execution shall state the reasons for applying for execution, the matters, the subject matter of execution, and the property status of the person subject to execution known to the applicant.
If the applicant for execution has genuine difficulty in writing the application, he or she may make an oral application. The reception personnel of the People's Court shall make a record of the oral application, which shall be signed or sealed by the applicant.
If a foreign party applies for execution, it shall submit a written application for execution in Chinese. If the judicial assistance treaty concluded between the country of the party and China or jointly acceded to by both has special provisions, such treaty provisions shall apply.
(2) A copy of the effective legal instrument.
(3) Identity certificate of the applicant for execution. If a natural person applies, he or she shall produce a resident identity card; if a legal person applies, it shall submit a copy of the legal person's business license and the identity certificate of its legal representative; if an unincorporated organization applies, it shall submit a copy of its business license and the identity certificate of its principal responsible person.
(4) If a successor or assignee of rights applies for execution, he or she shall submit certifying documents for succession or assignment of rights.
(5) Other documents or certificates that shall be submitted.

19. To apply for execution of an arbitration award made by an arbitration institution, a contract containing an arbitration clause or an arbitration agreement shall be submitted to the People's Court.
To apply for execution of an arbitration award made by a foreign arbitration institution, a Chinese-language version of the arbitration award that has been authenticated by a Chinese embassy or consulate stationed abroad or notarized by a Chinese notary organ shall be submitted.

20. An applicant for execution may entrust an agent to apply for execution on his or her behalf. Where an agent is entrusted, a power of attorney signed or sealed by the principal shall be submitted to the People's Court, stating the name of the agent, the matters entrusted, the scope of authority, and the time limit.
Where an entrusted agent abandons or modifies civil rights on behalf of the principal, or conducts execution settlement on behalf of the principal, or collects execution funds on behalf of the principal, the principal shall grant special authorization.

21. The collection of fees for execution applications shall be handled in accordance with the Measures for the Payment of Litigation Costs.

IV. Preparation Before Execution

22. A People's Court shall issue an execution notice within ten days after receiving the written application for execution or the written transfer for execution.
In addition to ordering the person subject to execution to perform the obligations determined in the legal instrument, the execution notice shall also notify him or her to bear the interest for delayed performance or the damages for delayed performance as provided in Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law.

23. Service of the execution notice shall be governed by the provisions of the Civil Procedure Law on service.

24. If the person subject to execution fails to perform the obligations determined in the effective legal instrument in accordance with the execution notice, execution measures shall be taken promptly.
When taking execution measures, the People's Court shall make corresponding legal instruments and serve them on the person subject to execution.

25. Where a People's Court executes an effective non-litigation legal instrument, it may, when necessary, retrieve case file materials from the institution that made the effective legal instrument.

V. Execution of Monetary Payments

26. Where a financial institution, without authorization, unfreezes funds frozen by a People's Court, causing the frozen funds to be transferred, the People's Court shall have the right to order it to recover the transferred funds within a specified period. If the funds cannot be recovered within the specified period, the People's Court shall rule that the financial institution shall bear liability to the applicant for execution with its own property to the extent of the transferred funds.

27. Where the person subject to execution is a financial institution, the deposit reserve and provision funds deposited by it with the People's Bank of China shall not be frozen or deducted or transferred, but its deposits with its own institution, other financial institutions, and its other deposits with the People's Bank of China may be frozen, transferred, or allocated, and other execution measures may be taken against other property of the person subject to execution; however, its business premises shall not be sealed up.

28. Where a natural person subject to execution has had his or her income converted into savings deposits, he or she shall be ordered to surrender the deposit certificates. If he or she refuses to surrender them, the People's Court shall make a ruling to withdraw his or her deposits, issue a notice of assistance in execution to the financial institution, and the financial institution shall withdraw the deposits of the person subject to execution and deliver them to the People's Court or deposit them into an account designated by the People's Court.

29. Where the income of the person subject to execution in a relevant unit has not yet been withdrawn, the People's Court shall make a ruling and issue a notice of assistance in execution to the unit, which shall assist in withholding or withdrawing the income.

30. Where a relevant unit, after receiving a notice from the People's Court to assist in executing the income of the person subject to execution, pays the income to the person subject to execution or other persons without authorization, the People's Court shall have the right to order it to recover the funds within a specified period; if it fails to recover the funds within the specified period, the People's Court shall rule that it shall bear liability to the applicant for execution to the extent of the amount paid.

31. With respect to property owned by the person subject to execution on which other persons enjoy mortgage rights, pledge rights, or lien rights, the People's Court may take sealing, seizure, or detention measures. After the property is auctioned or sold, the proceeds shall first satisfy the claims of the mortgagee, pledgee, or lienholder, and the remaining balance shall be used to satisfy the claims of the applicant for execution.

32. Where the person subject to execution or other persons dispose of property that has been sealed, seized, or frozen without authorization, the People's Court shall have the right to order the responsible person to recover the property within a specified period or to bear corresponding compensation liability.

33. Where the person subject to execution applies to sell on its own the property sealed by the People's Court, the People's Court may permit it, but shall supervise the sale at a reasonable price within the designated period and control the proceeds of the sale.

34. After the auction or sale of the property of the person subject to execution is concluded, the money and the property must be settled immediately.
The actual expenses incurred in entrusting an auction or organizing a sale of the property of the person subject to execution shall be deducted from the proceeds first. The portion of the proceeds exceeding the amount of the subject matter of execution and the execution expenses shall be returned to the person subject to execution.

35. Where the person subject to execution fails to perform the obligations determined in the effective legal instrument, the People's Court shall have the right to rule to prohibit the person subject to execution from transferring his or her intellectual property rights such as patent rights, exclusive rights to use registered trademarks, and copyright (the property rights part). Where the above rights have a registration administration authority, a notice of assistance in execution shall also be issued to the relevant authority, requiring it not to handle the transfer procedures of the property rights; when necessary, the person subject to execution may be ordered to surrender the certificates of property rights or rights of use to the People's Court for safekeeping.
With respect to the property rights mentioned in the preceding paragraph, execution measures such as auction and sale may be taken.

36. With respect to matured dividends or bonuses and other income that the person subject to execution is entitled to receive from a relevant enterprise, the People's Court shall have the right to rule to prohibit the person subject to execution from withdrawing such income and the relevant enterprise from paying it to the person subject to execution, and require the relevant enterprise to pay it directly to the applicant for execution.
With respect to expected dividends or bonuses and other income that the person subject to execution is entitled to receive from a relevant enterprise, the People's Court may take freezing measures, prohibiting the person subject to execution from withdrawing such income after maturity and the relevant enterprise from paying it to the person subject to execution. After maturity, the People's Court may withdraw the income from the relevant enterprise and issue a receipt for the withdrawal.

37. With respect to the share certificates (stocks) held by the person subject to execution in other joint-stock limited companies, the People's Court may detain them and compulsorily require the person subject to execution to transfer them in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Company Law; it may also directly dispose of them by auction or sale, or directly offset the stocks against the debts owed to the creditors, so as to satisfy the debts of the person subject to execution.

38. With respect to the investment rights and interests or equity interests of the person subject to execution in a limited liability company or other legal person enterprise, the People's Court may take freezing measures.
Where investment rights and interests or equity interests are frozen, the relevant enterprise shall be notified that it shall not handle transfer procedures for the frozen investment rights and interests or equity interests, and shall not pay dividends or bonuses to the person subject to execution. The person subject to execution shall not transfer the frozen investment rights and interests or equity interests on his or her own.

39. After the investment rights and interests owned by the person subject to execution in a legal person enterprise solely invested in by him or her are frozen, the People's Court may directly rule to transfer them, and use the proceeds from the transfer to satisfy his or her debts to the applicant for execution.
With respect to the frozen investment rights and interests or equity interests of the person subject to execution in a limited liability company, the People's Court may, in accordance with the provisions of Articles 71, 72, and 73 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, after obtaining the consent of more than half of all shareholders, auction, sell, or transfer them by other means. Shareholders who do not consent to the transfer shall purchase the transferred investment rights and interests or equity interests; if they do not purchase, they shall be deemed to consent to the transfer, which shall not affect the execution.
The People's Court may also permit and supervise the person subject to execution to transfer his or her investment rights and interests or equity interests on his or her own, and use the proceeds from the transfer to satisfy his or her debts to the applicant for execution.

40. Where a relevant enterprise, after receiving a notice of assistance in freezing issued by the People's Court, without authorization pays dividends or bonuses to the person subject to execution, or without authorization handles transfer procedures for the frozen equity interests for the person subject to execution, causing the transferred property to be irrecoverable, it shall bear liability to the applicant for execution to the extent of the dividends or bonuses paid or the value of the equity interests transferred.

VI. Execution of Delivery of Property and Performance of Acts

41. Where an effective legal instrument determines that the person subject to execution shall deliver a specific subject matter, the original item shall be executed. If the original item is concealed or illegally transferred, the People's Court shall have the right to order its surrender. If the original item has indeed been damaged or destroyed, compensation may be made by converting it into money with the consent of both parties.
If the two parties cannot reach consensus on compensation by conversion into money, the People's Court shall terminate the execution proceedings. The applicant for execution may file a separate lawsuit.

42. Where a relevant organization or individual holds the property or certificates designated for delivery in the legal instrument and, after receiving a notice of assistance in execution or a notice from the People's Court, cooperates with the person subject to execution in transferring the property or certificates, the People's Court shall have the right to order it to recover the property within a specified period; if it fails to recover the property within the specified period, the People's Court shall rule that it shall bear compensation liability.

43. Where, after the property of the person subject to execution is auctioned, sold, or offset against debt by ruling, the property needs to be delivered from its current possessor to the buyer or the applicant for execution, the provisions of Articles 249 and 250 of the Civil Procedure Law and Articles 41 and 42 of these Provisions shall apply.

44. Where the person subject to execution refuses to perform the acts specified in the effective legal instrument, the People's Court may compel him or her to perform them.
For acts that may be performed by substitute, a relevant unit or another person may be entrusted to complete them, and the expenses incurred in completing such acts shall be borne by the person subject to execution.
For acts that can only be performed by the person subject to execution, if the person subject to execution still refuses to perform after education, the People's Court shall handle the matter in accordance with the relevant provisions on acts obstructing execution.

VII. Execution of Matured Claims of the Person Subject to Execution

45. Where the person subject to execution is unable to clear his or her debts but enjoys matured claims against a third party other than the party to the case, the People's Court may, upon the application of the applicant for execution or the person subject to execution, issue a notice of performance of matured debts to the third party (hereinafter referred to as the "performance notice"). The performance notice must be served directly on the third party.
The performance notice shall contain the following contents:
(1) the third party shall directly perform the debts owed by it to the person subject to execution to the applicant for execution and shall not satisfy the debts to the person subject to execution;
(2) the third party shall perform the debts to the applicant for execution within fifteen days after receipt of the performance notice;
(3) if the third party has an objection to the performance of the matured debts, it shall raise the objection to the execution court within fifteen days after receipt of the performance notice;
(4) the legal consequences of the third party's violation of the above obligations.

46. An objection by the third party to the performance notice shall generally be raised in writing; if raised orally, the execution personnel shall record it in the transcript, and the third party shall sign or seal it.

47. Where the third party raises an objection within the period specified in the performance notice, the People's Court shall not enforce compulsorily against the third party and shall not review the objection raised.

48. A third party's claim that it has no capacity to perform or that it has no direct legal relationship with the applicant for execution shall not constitute an objection as referred to in these Provisions.
Where the third party acknowledges part of the debt and objects to part of it, compulsory execution may be carried out against the acknowledged part.

49. Where the third party fails to raise an objection within the period specified in the performance notice and also fails to perform, the execution court shall have the right to rule to enforce against it compulsorily. This ruling shall be served on the third party and the person subject to execution at the same time.

50. After the person subject to execution receives a performance notice from the People's Court, any act of abandoning his or her claims against the third party or delaying the time limit for the third party's performance shall be invalid, and the People's Court may still enforce against the third party where the third party raises no objection and fails to perform.

51. Where a third party, after receiving a notice from the People's Court requiring it to perform matured debts, performs to the person subject to execution without authorization, causing the property already performed to the person subject to execution to be irrecoverable, in addition to bearing joint and several liability for discharge with the person subject to execution to the extent of the property performed, the third party may be investigated for liability for obstructing execution.

52. After a ruling for compulsory execution is made against the third party, if the third party indeed has no property available for execution, compulsory execution shall not be carried out against the matured claims enjoyed by the third party against others.

53. After the third party has performed the debts to the applicant for execution in accordance with the performance notice of the People's Court or has been subjected to compulsory execution, the People's Court shall issue relevant certificates.

VIII. Execution Guarantee

54. Where, during the period of trial of a case, a surety provides a guarantee for the person subject to execution and the People's Court accordingly does not take preservation measures against the property of the person subject to execution or lifts the preservation measures, if after the case is concluded the person subject to execution has no property available for execution or his or her property is insufficient to clear the debts, even if the effective legal instrument does not determine that the surety shall bear liability, the People's Court shall have the right to rule to execute the property of the surety within the scope of the guarantee liability.

IX. Multiple Creditors Applying for Execution Against One Debtor and Participation in Distribution

55. Where multiple creditors, as determined by multiple effective legal instruments with content of monetary payment, apply separately for execution against the same person subject to execution, and none of the creditors holds a security interest in the subject matter of execution, they shall be satisfied in the order of the time when the execution court took execution measures.
Where the types of claims of multiple creditors are different, claims based on ownership and security interests shall be satisfied in preference to monetary claims. Where there are multiple security interests, satisfaction shall be made in the order of the establishment of the security interests.
Where multiple creditors, as determined by one effective legal instrument with content of monetary payment, apply for execution against the same person subject to execution, and the property subject to execution is insufficient to clear all debts, and none of the creditors holds a security interest in the subject matter of execution, satisfaction shall be made in proportion to their respective claims.

56. The specific distribution of the property of the person subject to execution shall be presided over by the court that first sealed, seized, or froze the property.
If the execution measures taken by the court that first sealed, seized, or froze were for the purpose of executing a property preservation ruling, the specific distribution shall be conducted after the trial of the case by that court is concluded.

11. Suspension, Termination, Conclusion of Cases, and Restitution in Execution
59. In a case that is brought up for trial or retried in accordance with the trial supervision procedure, the enforcement organ shall suspend execution in accordance with the ruling on suspension of execution made by the superior people's court or the court itself.
60. After the circumstances causing the suspension of execution have disappeared, the enforcement court may resume execution upon the application of a party or ex officio. Resumption of execution shall be notified to the parties in writing.
61. During execution, where the party subject to enforcement is declared bankrupt by a ruling of the People's Court, the enforcement court shall, in accordance with the provisions of Item (6) of Article 257 of the Civil Procedure Law, rule to terminate the execution.
62. A written ruling on suspension or termination of execution shall state the reasons and legal basis for the suspension or termination.
63. When a People's Court enforces an effective legal instrument, it shall generally conclude the enforcement case within six months from the date of filing the case, but the period during which execution is suspended shall be excluded. If special circumstances genuinely require an extension, the president of the court shall approve it.
64. The manners of concluding an enforcement case are:
(1) enforcement completed;
(2) termination of the current enforcement procedure;
(3) termination of enforcement;
(4) cancellation of the case;
(5) refusal to enforce;
(6) rejection of the application.
65. During or after enforcement, if the legal instrument on the basis of which enforcement is conducted is revoked or altered by the People's Court or other relevant authorities, the original enforcement organ shall, in accordance with the provisions of Article 233 of the Civil Procedure Law, upon the application of a party or ex officio, make a ruling for restitution in execution in accordance with the new effective legal instrument, ordering the original applicant for execution to return the property and its fruits that have been obtained. If the original applicant refuses to return, compulsory execution shall be applied.
Restitution in execution shall be filed as a new case, and the relevant provisions on execution procedures shall apply.
66. When restitution in execution is carried out, if the subject matter already executed is a specific thing, the original thing shall be returned. Where the original thing cannot be returned, compensation may be made at an assessed price with the consent of both parties.
Where the parties fail to reach an agreement on compensation at an assessed price, the People's Court shall terminate the restitution in execution procedure. The applicant for execution may bring a separate lawsuit.

12. Coordination of Execution Disputes
67. Where two or more People's Courts have a dispute in enforcing related cases, they shall resolve it through consultation. If consultation fails, they shall report level by level to the superior people's court until the common superior people's court is requested to coordinate and handle the matter.
If an execution dispute cannot be resolved through consultation by the Higher People's Courts, the relevant Higher People's Courts shall, in writing, request the Supreme People's Court to coordinate and handle the matter.
68. During enforcement, if it is discovered that two courts in different places, or a People's Court and an arbitration institution, have issued legal instruments with different adjudicative contents on the same legal relationship, the relevant courts shall immediately stop enforcement and report to the common superior people's court for handling.
69. When coordinating and handling an execution dispute case, if a superior people's court deems it necessary, it may decide to transfer the relevant funds to an account designated by the court.
70. The courts concerned must execute the handling decisions made by the superior people's court in coordinating execution disputes between lower people's courts.

13. Enforcement Supervision
71. Superior people's courts shall supervise the enforcement work of lower people's courts according to law. The Supreme People's Court shall supervise the enforcement work of local people's courts at all levels and special courts according to law.
72. Where a superior people's court finds that a ruling, decision, notice, or specific enforcement act made or taken by a lower people's court during enforcement is improper or erroneous, it shall promptly instruct the lower people's court to correct it, and may notify the relevant court to temporarily suspend enforcement.
Upon receipt of the instruction of the superior people's court, the lower people's court must immediately correct it. If it considers the instruction of the superior people's court erroneous, it may, within five days after receipt of the instruction, request the superior people's court for reconsideration.
Where the superior people's court considers the reasons for requesting reconsideration unfounded, and the lower people's court still fails to correct, the superior people's court may directly make a ruling or decision to correct it, serve it on the relevant court and the parties, and may directly issue a notice of assistance in enforcement to the relevant entity.
73. Where a superior people's court finds that a non-litigation effective legal instrument enforced by a lower people's court has grounds for refusal of enforcement, and the lower people's court should make a ruling of refusal of enforcement according to law but fails to do so, the superior people's court may order the lower people's court to make a ruling within a specified time limit, and may directly rule to refuse enforcement when necessary.
74. Where a superior people's court finds that a lower people's court (1) has failed to conclude an enforcement case (including a case entrusted for enforcement) within the prescribed period, (2) has failed to make a ruling, decision, or notice that it should make, or (3) has failed to take a specific enforcement act that it should take according to law, the superior people's court shall urge the lower people's court to enforce within a time limit, promptly make relevant rulings and other legal instruments, or take corresponding measures.
For a case in which a lower people's court has long failed to conclude enforcement, if truly necessary, the superior people's court may decide to enforce it by itself or jointly with the lower people's court, or designate another court within its jurisdiction to enforce it.
75. Where a superior people's court, in supervising, guiding, or coordinating the enforcement of cases by a lower people's court, finds that the effective legal instrument on the basis of which enforcement is conducted is genuinely erroneous, it shall notify the lower people's court in writing to temporarily suspend enforcement, and handle the matter in accordance with the trial supervision procedure.
76. Where a superior people's court decides to temporarily suspend the enforcement of an effective legal instrument during the period of review of a petition case, the relevant adjudication division shall send a copy of the notice of temporary suspension of enforcement to the enforcement organ.
77. Where a superior people's court notifies temporary suspension of enforcement, it shall at the same time specify the period of temporary suspension. The period of temporary suspension shall generally not exceed three months. Where special circumstances require extension, it shall be reported for approval to the president of the court, and the lower people's court shall be notified in a timely manner.
After the cause of temporary suspension is eliminated, the enforcement court shall be promptly notified to resume enforcement. If, upon expiration of the period, the superior people's court has not notified the continuation of the temporary suspension, the enforcement court may resume enforcement.
78. Where a lower people's court fails to enforce in accordance with the ruling, decision, or notice of a superior people's court, causing serious consequences, the relevant person in charge and the directly responsible person shall be held accountable in accordance with the relevant provisions.

14. Supplementary Provisions
79. These Provisions shall be implemented on a trial basis as of the date of promulgation.
Where any judicial interpretation previously made by this Court conflicts with these Provisions, these Provisions shall prevail. Matters not covered by these Provisions shall be handled in accordance with the previous provisions.
